sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OmO (oh-my-openagent) is a command-line AI agent for real work. You open a project, run omo and describe the job, and it researches, plans, writes code and checks the result, mixing different AI models for different parts of the task.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents often need hand-holding: you re-explain context, pick models and take the wheel back when they drift. OmO adds a planning mode called ultrawork, multi-agent runs, and a memory that reminds the agent of your past work.
whoFor: Developers who use terminal coding agents
Users with Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi or GLM subscriptions
People moving from the OpenCode edition
Power users who want multi-model agent runs
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want an opinionated agent that plans and verifies its own work, mixes frontier and cheap models, and keeps memory as Markdown in git.
requirements: A model subscription or API key

overview: Install the native omo binary with the install script, or with bun add -g omo-ai or npm i -g omo-ai (the npm package is omo-ai; the package called omo is unrelated). Then open your project, run omo and describe the job. OmO runs on senpi, the team's fork of the pi agent.

Adding ultrawork (or ulw) to a prompt makes the agent read the codebase, plan and verify each step. mass ulw splits a job into a graph of agents running on different models. A small model, Kibitzer, reads memory stored as Markdown files in git and nudges the main agent before it repeats a mistake.

Use /login for Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi and GLM subscriptions. Settings live in ~/.omo/omo.jsonc, with optional per-project .omo/omo.jsonc. OmO uses a Sustainable Use License, which is not an OSI open-source license.
